judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all four expectations with correct file/line citations; Report 2 is marginally stronger on expectation (a) because it unambiguously calls for deleting/removing the shadow-scoring sink and legacy billing secret rather than offering a replace-with-new-value alternative as Report 1 does.

report_1.evidence: ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"... AUTH_RELAXED = "true"... PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS = "qa@example.com:superadmin"... This seeds a QA superadmin backdoor account into the production system... The sink must be changed: set SHADOW_SCORING_SINK = "" if shadow scoring is not wanted in prod... LEGACY_BILLING_SECRET_ARN = "arn:synthetic:secrets:legacy-billing-key"... Production needs its own production-scoped secret ARN

report_2.evidence: ENABLE_DEBUG_TOOLBAR = "true"... Delete the key entirely... AUTH_RELAXED = "true"... Delete the key entirely... PRESET_ADMIN_ACCOUNTS = "qa@example.com:superadmin"... Delete the key entirely... Delete both keys entirely — an empty/absent sink is the only state that actually disables the write path... LEGACY_BILLING_SECRET_ARN... Do not recreate the legacy secret wiring in the new environment; delete the key.

report_1.evidence: VITE_-prefixed variables are inlined into the built bundle at build time... deploy-prod — explicitly named "deploy the same already-built digest to prod" (lines 34–35) — deploys the identical image to production... production users' browsers would call https://staging-api.example.com... The build-once-promote-by-digest design is otherwise good practice, but it is incompatible with baking environment-specific URLs in at build time; one of the two has to change.

report_2.evidence: Net effect: the production frontend ships with the staging API URL https://staging-api.example.com baked into its bundle, with no runtime way to fix it. Production traffic from real clinics would hit the staging API. Production needs its own build (--mode production with a .env.production carrying the prod API URL, or a runtime-injected config), not a promotion of the staging-built digest

report_1.evidence: Database setup and migrations are unaccounted for. docs/prod-runbook.md:6 promises "Database migrations are applied automatically during deploy," which can only live in the missing deploy.sh; the fresh production database needs migrations 0001_base → 0003_billing applied on first release, and no visible pipeline step does this.

report_2.evidence: No database migration step... docs/prod-runbook.md:6 claims "Database migrations are applied automatically during deploy," but the runbook flags itself "last updated: 3 months ago" ... and the committed pipeline contradicts it... For a first production release against a brand-new, empty database, an explicit migration run is required; "the pipeline succeeded" would not mean the schema exists.

report_1.evidence: infra/prod/main.tf:3 — oidc_sub_condition = "repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:staging". The production deploy role is configured to trust GitHub OIDC tokens from the staging environment. It must be "repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production".

report_2.evidence: the prod role's trust condition at infra/prod/main.tf:3 was copied unchanged and still reads repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:staging... The condition must be changed to repo:acme-health/medislot:environment:production so production has its own scoped trust, not one shared with staging.
